The person on the floor remains crouched or prone and does not resist, consistent with a one-sided assault. By 2.0s–3.0s, the aggressor stands up and moves away, while the victim remains seated on the floor, showing signs of distress or incapacitation. This sequence matches the defined anomaly: a one-sided attack where the victim is an able adult who is not fighting back.
